text.p: Swedish security company Securitas said on Tuesday it expected its 1997 profit development to be in line with previous years'.
"The profit development for the financial year is therefore expected to be in line with that of previous years," it said in its first quarter earnings statement.

The company posted a 1.6 percent rise in first quarter pre-tax profit to 124 million crowns compared to the corresponding year earlier quarter and earnings per share rose to 1.22 crowns from 1.21 crowns.

The Spanish cash-in-transit (CIT) operations -- which suffered a loss in volume of 60 million crowns on an annual basis -- and additional restructuring costs in Germany had a negative impact on the profit by somewhat less than 10 million crowns, the company said.
"The effects of lost volume in Spain and restructuring of the German operations will gradually diminish as measures instituted take effect," the group said.
Sales rose 14 percent to 2.42 billion crowns in the first quarter. In local currencies, pre-tax profit was flat while the sales rise was the same, the company said.
"Acquisitions, mainly of Security Express in Britain, have increased sales by 10 percent (while) organic growth for the period was four percent," Securitas said.
Operating profit after amortization of goodwill rose slightly to 132.4 million crowns from 131.4 million.
The Nordic countries posted continued good development in terms of volume as well as profits, Securitas said.
In the newly acquired businesses, restructuring of previously unprofitable operations is under way and being completed, it said.
"Experience tells us that some parts of this work may take longer than anticipated, while other parts are completed quicker," the company said.
"Overall, these acquisitions are developing in accordance with our expectations, however."
